title: Job The Black Prophet And Our People Today

sense.text: “I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.” When Job said he’s a brother to dragons, his friends represented something. That isn’t touched on in full today, only a little about his friends.

“My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.” The forefather, the prophet Job, said my skin is black upon me. Type in the prophet Job on Google under images and they got Job as an Edomite, and believe it or not there are Israelite camps that teach Job was an Edomite because he dwelt in the land of Uz. Job was not an Edomite.

You’ve heard Christians say it doesn’t mean his color, it’s taken out of context, it means his demeanor. Really? Is that what that means? The revised and expanded Holman Illustrated Bible Dictionary, page 224, under black: ‘often used to denote the color of physical objects’, hair, and it names Job 30:30. So the scholars know Job 30:30 is referring to skin, just as the Song of Solomon and Lamentations do.

The catacombs were a range of underground tombs throughout Rome and Italy that the Jews built or used as places of refuge and places of meeting, because there was a great persecution against the Jews. They were carved out of rock by the Israelites. Job appears about a dozen times in the catacomb paintings, usually a solitary seated figure, sometimes with his wife offering him food on a rod or stick and not touching him because of the loathsome sores that afflict him. The whole book is in black and white, but look at the color of his skin: his legs, his hands, his face compared to the rest of the painting. Our forefathers that were in those catacombs painted the forefather Job on the tombs. My skin is black.

The same walls show Christ enthroned between Peter and Paul: look at that black man. The prophet Micah, black on the stones. Abraham preparing to sacrifice Isaac: baby Isaac a black boy. Moses striking the rock, and Christ multiplying the loaves, portrayed as a black man, and the disciples carrying the loaves in their hands are all black, everybody black with afros. Daniel in the lions’ den, black. Tobias with his fish and the angel: Tobias is black and the angel Raphael is black. That’s in the Apocrypha that white Christians today say is not canon, but our fathers used the Apocrypha. They put the book in black and white to be cunning and slick.

Inside a cathedral in Russia, black people are all around the walls: Christ, Joseph, Christ’s daddy, the black angel, King David with the crown on his head, all the Saints of Israel on the ceiling. And at the bottom: Job on the garbage dump, the forefather Job, a black man. Don’t tell me there was a fire and it burned every place else but his loincloth.

These books are not going to be put in your African-American book section. Expand your way of thinking and go to the Jewish book section, the Byzantine section, the Middle Ages section, the archaeology section. In the Black book sections all you get is Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X, Sojourner Truth and slavery, nothing else. The Christian community wants you to think it’s a figment of your imagination, that they’re really white and you’re under the influence. No, you’re under the spell called Christianity, white supremacy Christianity. That’s why we don’t entertain Christianity and don’t indulge in stupidity from Christians: anything we show them, they close their eyes like them three dumb monkeys, see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil. Christians don’t know a dag gone thing.

This is the calamity of the forefather Job. Satan, the spiritual demon Satan in heaven, having a conversation with the Most High: “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” “But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.” If you let me touch this dude, he will curse you to your face.
“Behold, all that he hath is in thy power”: the Lord allowed Satan to touch Job. “Only upon himself put not forth thine hand”: but upon Job himself, don’t put your hands on him.

This is the first thing Satan did against Job. “And the Sabeans fell upon them”: write this down, the Sabeans are Somalia, Somalians. They “slain the servants with the edge of the sword”: the Sabeans killed Job’s servants. “The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants”: more of his servants and Job’s sheep got burnt up. “The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away”.

Write this down: the first three things Satan took from Job were his source of income, which was his business and his goods. We’re reading this because some of you may be able to relate to it, and it relates to us as a people.

“Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead”. Job’s sons and daughters were taken from him.

Remember, Job was a real person, but his life shows the similitudes of the 12 tribes of Israel today.

precepts.why: What happened to us: “The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. Our source of income, our goods, would be taken from us, prophetically.

“All thy trees and fruit of thy land shall the locust consume.” Didn’t we just read about the fire that came from heaven and burnt up what Job had? It seems very similar.

“The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.” We as a nation, as a people, would have nothing. That’s what the prophecy is saying.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. You know what it means, for the abundance of all things? We had the earth in our possession, everything was ours, and it was taken from us like that. Why? Because of our own disobedience.

So just like Job lost his source of income, as a people we lost it too. He lost his goods, so did we. He lost his businesses, so did we.

“That all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. “Cursed shalt thou be in the city”: whatever city we would dwell in as a people, we’d be cursed, having nothing. “And cursed shalt thou be in the field”: whatever fields we were in, we’d be cursed, picking tobacco, things of that nature; the images show us cursed in the field. “Cursed shall be thy basket and thy store”: our source of income would be cursed. “Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body”: our children. “And the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine”: kine is your cattle, “and the flocks of thy sheep.”

So just as it was taken from Job, it was taken from us as a people.
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” Just like Job lost his sons and daughters, so did we lose ours.

“The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword”, meaning killed. “Thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, and not pitied.” So our sons and daughters were killed, and our sons and daughters have gone into captivity, the same as what we’re reading about Job.

sense.text: “Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.”

“So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” It’s very similar: what Job went through, we as a people are going through.

precepts.why: The one about sickness: “Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee. Also every sickness, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, them will the Lord bring upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” Very similar to what Job went through, we as a people are going through.

“I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me”: that’s what the Lord is saying to our people. “The ox knoweth his owner”: as dumb as an ox is, he knows who his owner is. “And the ass his master’s crib”: as dumb as an ass is, you could put an ass a mile away and he could find his way home to his master’s crib. “But Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider”: we don’t know who our creator is, we don’t know our homeland and we don’t know our identity. That’s what that’s saying.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” “Ye will revolt more and more”.

Watch this: “the whole head is sick”, the whole head of the nation of Israel is sick, “and the whole heart faint.” “From the sole of the foot even unto the head”, from the sole of the foot of the Twelve Tribes of Israel even unto the head, “there is no soundness in it”. Just like there was no soundness in the forefather Job, there’s no soundness in the 12 tribes of Israel: “but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores”, just like Job had. “They have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.”

“Your country is desolate”: our homeland is desolate. “Your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.”

sense.text:
Job lost everything, right? But look what Satan left him with: his wife. She didn’t get killed with the kids. “Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” You can’t make this stuff up. Curse God and die: look at you, you’re sick, you’re on your last legs, die. Let it go.

Now back to his wife: his wife is our wife.

Although he was sick and jacked up, Job ain’t take no mess from her. “But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh”: woman, you sound stupid as hell. “Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” You was with me when God blessed us with homes, houses, source of income, you was good; but now that I lost everything, including my health? “In all this did not Job sin with his lips.”

precepts.why: “Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him”: Job’s mindset was though God slay him, yet will I trust in him. “But I will maintain mine own ways before him.” Job maintained his ways; he kept his integrity. That’s what you need to understand.

“Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.” This is Christ saying this through the prophet. You might ask, why can’t I tell my wife everything? Biblically, there are certain situations to hold all that. Keep your mouth shut; you ain’t got to tell her everything. Samson had a simp spirit on him and it cost him dearly. Now, not all women are wicked, that’s not what’s being said, but Christ said don’t tell her everything.

You get into a marriage, telling your wife you got this set up, you got that set up, and she’s like, oh yeah, really, and she’s just biding her time. Not all women, not all. She waits for the opportune time and says I’ve been thinking about this, I want a divorce, and half of all the things you got I’m going to take. How does she know you got those things, brothers? Because you had to be a big mouth, a blabbermouth, and you told her everything. There have been several instances here in IUIC: brothers so hot you had to go get married, and she took you to the cleaners. She made sure what you got: a good job, what else you got. Your head is on her knees, she waited some time, took you to court, and now you are struggling working in McDonald’s. Learn from these classes; everybody in here is not Sarah. Here I am in the hospital all jacked up and my wife is asking what you got laid to the side for me? Don’t worry about it. When I’m dead you’ll know, not before. I ain’t telling you nothing.

“For the son dishonoureth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother”: y’all are seeing this today. “A man’s enemies are the men of his own house”: that’s what Christ said, what the Son of God said. “Therefore I will look unto the Lord; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.” The only one we can trust in, brothers, is the Most High.

“Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise”. Believe it or not, some of your wives are waiting for you to drop dead and die. Not all, but some. We’ve seen it here: as soon as the brother died, she had a Christian funeral, praise white Jesus. You can’t make this stuff up. “When I sit in darkness, the Lord shall be a light unto me. I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.”

Watch this: “Then she that is mine enemy shall see it”. She been waiting for you to drop dead and die. “And shame shall cover her which said unto me, Where is the Lord thy God?” This is what Job’s wife said, which is what some of your wives say: where’s the Lord your God? Brothers, don’t worry; some of y’all are going through it because you got Job’s wife. “Mine eyes shall behold her: now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.” She gonna get what she deserves: trodden down like mud in the street. Dead, because she don’t believe in God, she don’t believe in this truth.

The proof that it is Christ: “Of which salvation the prophets have enquired and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that should come unto you: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify”, the spirit of Christ which was in the prophets, “when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.”

So when we’re teaching and you hear us say Christ said this, Christ said that, and we’re in the book of Micah or the Book of Job, that is Christ speaking through them.

Keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom: this is Samson and Delilah. “And she made him sleep upon her knees”: she put Samson to sleep upon her knees, “and she called for a man, and she caused him to shave off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.” Delilah sexed Samson so good she made him fall asleep on her knees, and because he told her everything, she used it against him to destroy him.

Read above it: “When she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, so that his soul was vexed unto death; That he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me”.

Let’s see if things changed in the New Testament. Some of you think you got a good wife; some of the sisters are legitimately good, but there are some. This week there was a video of a brother and wife here fist fighting in the house: she grabbed the baby, he’s trying to snatch the baby, she called the cops, she gets him arrested, he in jail. You can’t make this stuff up.

“For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.” Christ ain’t coming for peace in the house. Why? Because some are going to believe and some are not; that’s what it means. “And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.” Didn’t we just read that in Micah 7? Christ was speaking that through Micah; now he’s saying it for himself.

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me”. Some of you love your parents more than the Lord. Sisters have come and said I married a mama’s boy. Sister, you knew he was a mama’s boy before you got with him: he spoke to his mama every damn day, your argument with him his mama know about it, she call you and cuss you out. He’s not the type to marry. Brother, you know she love her mama and daddy more than you; she set it up so y’all get a place living near her parents, and they’re right there in all your business. You’re not worthy of the Lord God.

“And he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me”. Some of you sisters idolize your children; you love them kids more than Christ, you’re not worthy of him, you can’t be Christ’s disciple. If you love your kids, let them rebel against this truth and they will get you locked up. We have seen it from New York to Texas: my parents abused me, they forced me to keep God’s commandments and I don’t want to keep it. Click click, now you in jail. Y’all keep playing with them kids. They’re cute right now, some of y’all got adorable kids, but just wait till they get a little older and you’ll see if they for the Lord or for this world. Sometimes it depends on what mama is teaching them; sometimes they just pure demons.

“And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.” That means you have to be willing to risk your life, to give your life, to sacrifice your life for this truth. Some of you will, some of you won’t.

“He that findeth his life shall lose it”: when persecution comes you step back, you don’t want no parts of it, you want to save your life. Christ said you’re going to lose it: you’re going to get thermonuclear fire, the Lake of Fire. “And he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it”: that goes back to the cross in verse 38. If you give up your life for this truth, you’re gonna have eternal life. That’s what the Son of God says.

The Book of Job never says what Job did with his wife, whether he kept her and put her in check and she followed, or he got rid of her. The Lord left it open, because everybody’s situation may be a little bit different. Some women you can correct: sis, you sound stupid, don’t say that no more, and she says okay, I’m sorry, my lord. Some of y’all got wives that say drop dead, curse God and die, when you sick and can’t do nothing.

“And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets”: Christ speaking through Solomon finds more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, like Delilah. “And her hands as bands”: trying to trap you up from God, trying to keep you from the word of God. “Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”: brother, if you want to please God, you’ll leave a woman like that. Escape means get the hell away.

“But the sinner shall be taken by her”: the simp. Oh, she’s the love of my life; I know she hate God and hate me, I know she smacked me upside the head, I know she called me a no-good dirty ass at times, but I love her, that’s my baby. God says the sinner shall be taken by her. The simple brother will never work up the courage to move the hell on and get the hell away from her; he’ll always have an excuse, a reason, I’m gonna do this, I’m gonna fix that. She ain’t changing. And it don’t matter how much muscles you got: the biggest and strongest brothers are the weakest of you all, big on the outside but real petite on the inside. A seven foot simp.

sense.text:
The question sometimes comes up, was Job real? Yes, the prophet Job was real, and he was part of the holy seed. God compares Job with people like Daniel and Noah; that’s how you know he was real.

“When the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof, and will send famine upon it, and will cut off man and beast from it”. The prophecy is God will send famine. The pictures of famine on the continent show it: this is what Christ, through Ezekiel, said he would send upon the children of Israel, and those are images from the continent for a reason. Write down number one: famine.

“Though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it”: he puts them all in the same category. So Job could not have been an Edomite, who God hates. Not only is he black, God compares him with Noah and Daniel. Stop listening to stupid Black Hebrew Israelite camps who don’t know a damn thing.

In it, in the famine: “they should deliver but their own souls by their righteousness”. They can only deliver their own souls by their righteousness.

Number two: “If I cause noisome beasts to pass through the land, and they spoil it, so that it be desolate, that no man may pass through because of the beasts”: these wild animals. Though these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, were in it, “they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters”: they couldn’t save their sons, they could not save their daughters. “They only shall be delivered, but the land shall be desolate.”

In South Africa they sicced the dogs on them. The Jerusalem Post, published 2020: ‘South African Jew: we cannot sit out today’s fight against racism.’ Crescent International: ‘experience of apartheid.’ Just like they did over here, same thing. What the Bible talked about is true on the continent of Africa.

“Or if I bring a sword upon that land”: a sword means war. “Sword, go through the land; so that I cut off man and beast from it”. Though Noah, Daniel and Job were in it, “they shall deliver neither sons nor daughters”. The Lord is stressing it because some of you think you can save your sons and daughters. No, you can’t. They’re real cute right now, adorable, but around 10 they start making their own little decisions, and you’re gonna see if they for the Lord or for the devil. “But they only shall be delivered themselves.”

Examples of the sword on the continent of Africa: the Biafra war in Nigeria, thousands upon thousands of people killed. Five Ghanaians killed in South Africa in the xenophobic attacks, a man set on fire, burning alive.

“Or if I send a pestilence into that land”, meaning disease, “and pour out my fury upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast: Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it”, in the pestilence, “they shall deliver neither son nor daughter”. Even they, as righteous as they are, could not save son or daughter. “They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.” Disease is running rampant throughout the continent of Africa: Ebola, zika, a lot of different things out there.

“How much more when I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sword, and the famine, and the noisome beast, and the pestilence”. Write it down: God’s four sore judgments are one, famine; two, beast; three, the sword, which is war; four, pestilence, which is disease.

precepts.why: Their righteousness: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” That’s our righteousness: keeping God’s commandments.

sense.text: Now you might say to yourself, that’s old time in the Bible, back then. Revelation is the revealing of what’s to come. “And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth beast say, Come and see.”

“And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death”. This death is Esau, the so-called white man. “And Hell followed with him”: wherever this man go, hell follows behind him. “And power was given unto them”: death and hell is talking about a nation of men. “Over the fourth part of the earth”: the book The Fourth Part of the World, ‘the race to the ends of the earth and the epic story of the map that gave America its name’, by Toby Lester, lets you know America is the fourth part of the earth. Power over America, to do what? It’s the same four judgments.

“To kill with sword”: write that down. On this side of the world, the fourth part of the earth, there was slaughter, bodies thrown into huge open graves. Thousands upon thousands of our people died during World War One; they like to make believe we didn’t exist during World War One, but we did. Our people fought in World War Two and they put us in concentration camps, burned us in Auschwitz and places like that, but nobody wants to talk about that. The Persian Gulf: our people was always fighting in America’s wars. That’s the sword. The white man kills with sword.

“And with hunger”: that’s famine. Our people being killed with hunger, food shortages, this is America. It’s gonna escalate; it’s happening in certain parts of the country, and we’ve been warning y’all about this for a long time.

“And with death”: that’s disease. This is what happened to our brother Rasheem Carter. White folks killed him. First they said animals attacked him and did that, but you could tell a steel or iron instrument did that; animals don’t do that. A lot of times black people only say stop murder by police, but the ones that killed Rasheem Carter were not the police, and the ones that killed Ahmaud Arbery were not the police. Many of our people are being killed, not just by the police. God tells us it’s Esau, Edom. These little fringe groups out here that say it’s just the police have an ulterior motive.

More death: ‘the most dangerous place for an African-American is in the womb.’ Black women don’t want to talk about that. The black woman has killed more of her people than anybody on the face of the earth; she has surpassed the Ku Klux Klan in the murder of her people. Black on black violence: black men out there in gangs killing one another. You got some Israelite camps the same way: they hate the truth, they hate one another, they hate to see Israel rising up in glory and honor and respect.

“And with the beasts of the earth.” Gator bait: during the time of chattel slavery and even a little after, they would take those cute adorable little kids, put them by the side of the river with a rope around their torso, so when the alligators came and swallowed them they pulled the alligator to shore and killed it to make shoes, belts, hats and gloves. They made a candy out of it, little African, a dainty morsel, licorice drops. Growing up you would see these things and never understand what you were looking at; our parents couldn’t tell us. It wasn’t until coming into the truth that you find out. The NAACP made public a dispatch from the Louisville, Kentucky Herald that colored babies were being used as alligator bait in the vicinity of Chipley, Florida, the price paid to colored mothers said to be two dollars. Two dollars for your baby. And they made jokes out of it, little caricatures making mockery of our children being put to death by beasts, like the Bible said, on the fourth part of the earth, on this side. During the turbulent 60s they would sic their canine dogs on us in the Civil Rights Movement; here in Atlanta they let the dog out on a young lady and it tore her up. That’s what the Bible’s talking about.

Not only that, they use beasts for other things: to create the pestilence. They use DNA from animals and splice it together with human DNA to create these diseases. A woman who used to work with Dr. Anthony Fauci: when she first blew his spot up he had her arrested and she went to jail for several years. She said she helped create the AIDS disease with Fauci and a whole bunch of scientists, Ebola, and she put it all out there; they took all her YouTube videos down, every last one, and took her medical license, everything. Not that she love our people, but she wanted to expose the evil she was a part of. That’s the prophecy of Revelation 6:7-8.

precepts.why:
“Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. Let’s talk about a particular race of man on earth. What does it mean, lifted up? He lifted himself up as God, as Christ, as the angels. This is your friendly neighborhood white man. His soul is not upright in him; you cannot conform him. “But the just shall live by his faith”: we’re gonna live by Christ.

“Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine”: the wine is philosophy. “He is a proud man”: that’s how you know it’s the white man. That proud man is Esau, Edom. “Neither keepeth at home”: he don’t stay at home. “Who enlargeth his desire as hell, and is as death”: God says he is as death, the same Death on the pale horse. “And cannot be satisfied”: this man cannot be satisfied. “But gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people”: that’s pinpointing America. All nations and kindreds is here in America.

About the wine: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine”. So wine represents the spirit of falsehood and lying, and that is how the proud man of Habakkuk 2:5 transgresses.

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: Edom is the so-called white man. “We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle”: the nations are going to rise up against Edom in battle. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Here come the pride: “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. That is the proud man, the man that sits on the pale horse.

“Woe is me! woe is me! who will deliver me in those days?” The prophet Ezra said who will deliver me in those days. “The beginning of sorrows and great mournings; the beginning of famine and great death; the beginning of wars, and the powers shall stand in fear; the beginning of evils! what shall I do when these evils shall come?”

“Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as scourges for amendment.” It’s the same four, brothers; it’s the same four, sisters. The Lord has smitten our people with famine, plague, tribulation, things of that nature, “But for all these things they shall not turn from their wickedness, nor be alway mindful of the scourges.” A lot of us forgot about the 60s with the canine dogs; we see them attacking and we forget about it. Covid-19 just happened and we’ve already forgotten about it; many of us went back to eating garbage, you know who you are.

“Behold, victuals shall be so good cheap upon earth”: you say oh yeah, Walmart, Costco, everything’s cheap. The Bible’s talking about our people: “that they shall think themselves to be in good case”. A lot of you think you’re good now, all this is past. “And even then shall evils grow upon earth, sword, famine, and great confusion. For many of them that dwell upon earth shall perish of famine; and the other, that escape the hunger, shall the sword destroy.”

So the Lord got it all laid out for us, and that goes right back to Revelation 6:8. Many of us are in this truth playing games with the prophecies God has laid out for us. You do yourself, and your children if you have any, a disservice.

sense.text:
“Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord”: all of us, men and women, let us all be patient for the coming of the Lord God.

“Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth”: the husbandman is the man that plants crops. He plants seed today, and he’s got to wait till that particular season comes for that seed to sprout and grow. So he “hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain”: the early crops at the beginning of the season and the crops at the end of the season.

“Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts”: James is telling us we got to be patient like that husbandman, just like that. “For the coming of the Lord draweth nigh”: it comes near. Understand that thing.

“Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned.” The root of a grudge is hatred. You got many Israelite camps who have a grudge against Israel United in Christ, not that we’ve done anything to them, but because God is showing us favor and not them: ‘y’all are getting the audience, y’all are getting the people… let’s set up camp right next to them, let’s do something evil against them.’ These camps that have grudges against us for no reason will be condemned by God.

So brothers, we can’t roll like that. We are the sons and daughters of God; we can’t have grudges. Those are our brothers, those are our sisters.

It goes for husband and wife too. When you’re single and in a congregation holding grudges, you will be condemned. When you get married and have a grudge against your spouse, you will be condemned. Israelite camp, you have a grudge against another camp, you will be condemned.

“Behold, the judge standeth before the door”: the Lord is the judge, and he stands before the door.

“Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience”: consider the prophets who have spoken and prophesied in the name of the Lord, as an example of suffering affliction and of patience. Like who? Like the forefather Job.

“Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job”: he gives you an example in case you couldn’t think of one.

“And have seen the end of the Lord”: you saw what the Lord did at the end, and we’re going to touch on that. “That the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.” So we got to remember Job in this truth, brothers and sisters: how the Lord was very merciful and pitiful upon Job.

precepts.why:
Here’s more examples. “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also.” Why would Christ say that through the prophet Paul? “Knowing that tribulation worketh patience”: that’s why. Tribulation teaches us patience.

We all lack patience. We want it now, we want it today. We got to be like that husbandman who plants his crops today and has to wait to the end of the season for the crop to grow up. The Lord says you got to learn patience, and in order for you to learn patience, brother, sister, you got to go through tribulation.

“And patience, experience”: patience teaches us experience. A lot of you got experience in the world, but the Lord don’t care about that. He wants to know about your experience in this truth. What have you done for the Lord in this truth? Where’s your tribulation in this truth, your patience, your experience in this truth?

“And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed”: once your hope is built up you will not be ashamed, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.” The spirit of the Lord gives us that Holy Spirit, shed abroad in our hearts, that we learn patience, experience and hope, and all that comes through tribulation. There’s a purpose behind tribulation. There was a purpose behind Job’s tribulation.

“Confirming the souls of the disciples”: our job is to confirm your souls as well. “And exhorting them to continue in the faith”: our job is to exhort every man and every woman in this truth to continue in this faith. Do not leave this truth. Don’t let it be another 2018, and all them people now are trying to come back. You don’t want to be in that number.

“And that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” Why? Because tribulation teaches us patience, and patience teaches us experience, and experience teaches us hope. There’s a domino effect to the tribulation; it’s a building process.

sense.text:
“For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom”: guess what, brothers, guess what, sisters, that falls under the sword we were reading earlier. Sword is war.

“And there shall be famines”: didn’t we read that famine is going to come? Christ is talking about the same four judgments. “And pestilences”: that’s disease. It’s gonna cover this place. We’ve experienced it like a woman in travail, here a little, there a little. Now the disease has come and gone, and ‘we good now, we could go back to being’ the same. No, you better wake up.

The same thing Ezekiel said, the same thing Ezra said, the same thing John the Revelator said, is the same thing Christ is saying here.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you”: the men and women in this truth. They shall deliver us up to be afflicted and shall kill us.

“And ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” There is a campaign against us, saying we’re a hate group, we’re racist, we murdered people in Jersey: lie, lie, lie. They’re building a campaign to stop the sons and daughters of God.

“And then shall many be offended”: some of you are going to be offended at this. “And shall betray one another”: some of you are going to betray us, and we know that. “And shall hate one another”: some of you gonna turn and hate us.
“And many false prophets shall rise”: those are your preachers, your imams, your popes, your reverends. “And shall deceive many”: they’re going on a deceptive campaign.
“Because iniquity shall abound”: some of you are gonna stop keeping God’s commandments. You’re going to see sin on the rise.

“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” Hear what the Messiah said. Endure what? Start at verse 7: sword, famine, pestilence and beasts. We got to endure that. From verse 7 down, the affliction is going to come, and Christ said he that endures to the end is going to be saved.

So you got to go through. That’s what Acts 14:22 said: we must through much tribulation enter the kingdom.

precepts.why:
“Thou therefore endure hardness.” What hardness? Sword, famine, pestilence and beasts, those four sore judgments, which also includes the afflictions that are going to come. Christ said he that shall endure until the end shall be saved, and the hardness is that tribulation.

“As a good soldier of Jesus Christ”: because we are good soldiers of Jesus Christ. “No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

“Whosoever remaineth from all these that I have told thee shall escape, and see my salvation, and the end of your world.” There’s a remnant chosen that’s going to live to the end. You’re going to see the end of this world, and God’s salvation.

“He that shall endure the peril in that time”: welcome to the word, endure, endure, endure. Another word for peril is tribulation.

“Hath kept himself: they that be fallen into danger are such as have works, and faith toward the Almighty.” They that have fallen into danger: that danger is the tribulation of war, famine, beasts and pestilence.

sense.text: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” So you men and women, when you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation. That temptation in verse 1 is the adversity in verse 5.
“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure”: constantly endure, endure, endure. “And make not haste in time of trouble”: don’t run, don’t run, don’t leave this truth.
“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

Listen good to this: “Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully.” Romans 5:3 said we glory in tribulation; now here it says take it cheerfully.

“And be patient when thou art changed to a low estate”: be patient when you ain’t got nothing, when your source of income is gone, your business is ruined, destroyed, like we just read about in Job earlier.

“For gold is tried in the fire”: you men and women, you are the gold God is looking at. He’s trying you; he must try you. God wants to make you into gold, but in order to do that he’s got to try us.

“And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity”: only acceptable men and acceptable women are chosen in the furnace of adversity. You’re not just going to tell the Lord ‘oh, I believe’ and that’s it. God says I got to try you, I got to try your faith, I got to put you through tribulation.

So write this word down: what we’ve read, THAT, will either make you or break you. The T stands for tribulation, the H for hardness, the A for adversity and the T for temptation. Going through that will either make us or break us. Some brothers and some sisters have been broken when they’ve gone through tribulation, hardness, adversity and temptation. They’re gone; we don’t see them no more. Some are on YouTube cursing us out like it’s our fault, what they went through. That’s not our fault. The Lord said he’s going to try you, and he meant that thing.

precepts.why:
Let me show you something. “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross.” Dross is something regarded as worthless: rubbish, debris, trash, garbage, foreign matter, dregs or mineral waste, in particular scum formed on the surface of molten metal. There’s something in all of us that’s worthless, garbage within us, and God said he will turn his hand upon us and purge it away, “and take away all thy tin.”

Now we know what the dross and the tin is: those evil thoughts we have, the evil eye, the hatred we have one for another, the thoughts of adultery, the thoughts of fornication, the lasciviousness. All of those things is the dross and the tin.

“And I will restore thy judges as at the first”: God wants to make us to be like the judges at the beginning, “and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.” We want to be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city. That is the gold tried in the fire.

Now he’s going to break down the garbage that’s in us. “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”: we got evil thoughts in us. “Adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness”: all of that is in us. “An evil eye”: that’s hatred for your brother, and it’s in us. “Blasphemy, pride, foolishness”: it’s in us.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” That’s the garbage, the dross and the tin God purges away in the furnace of adversity.

sense.text:
“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” Men, women, listen: what Christ said, to endure your tribulation, your hardness, your adversity and temptation, has nothing to do with motivation. Write that down.

People ask, ‘Bishop, how do you stay motivated?’ Nobody wakes up every day motivated, unless you’re on drugs. You have good days, you have bad days. Motivation is a driving force, and you don’t have that every day unless you are a supernatural being. Nobody is motivated every day from sun up to sundown; it’s impossible.

Enduring has nothing to do with being motivated 24/7, but it has everything to do with discipline. I’m not always motivated, but I’m always disciplined, and that’s how every man and every woman must be. Self-discipline is the number one trait essential to accomplishing goals. We want to make it to the end, we want to endure to the end, so we need discipline.

precepts.why:
“He hath mercy on them that receive discipline”: God has mercy on them that receive discipline, “and that diligently seek after his judgments.”

Discipline is what we need, brothers and sisters. I don’t care about depression; there’s too much in this Bible for us to be depressed. We must be disciplined. You might not wake up today wanting to go out to camp: you better go out and do it. You might not wake up wanting to eat your diet food today, lettuce and tomatoes, but you better eat it. You might not wake up wanting to lift weights or do a sit-up, but you got to do it, just like you got to wake up and take care of them children. It’s called discipline.

About diligence: “Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure.” That diligence is endure, endure. God don’t care about your motivation; he don’t give a damn about that. You best endure.

That’s what he’s telling every man and every woman: the Bishops, deacons, captains, officers, soldiers, men, women, all of us. Endure. I know I stepped on some toes.

sense.text: “Moreover Job continued his parable.” Brothers, you up-and-coming teachers, understand this: Job’s life, although it was real, was a parable for us, the nation of Israel, so that when we go through this captivity we can endure to the end and not give up.

“Let mine enemy be as the wicked”: we have enemies against this gospel that are our very own people. Job says let them be as the wicked, and the wicked is Edom.

So that’s men and women of our own race who despise this gospel, who hate this truth, who want to stop us from preaching and teaching the gospel: let them be as the wicked. “And he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.”

Never forget verse 7. The same judgment Esau is going to get, these nations, our wicked brothers and sisters are gonna get the same judgment.
“For what is the hope of the hypocrite”: that’s the proof that the enemy Job was talking about is the hypocrites of our people. “Though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?”

“Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?” Will God hear the cry of the hypocrite, the Israelite man, the Israelite woman who know they’re Israelites but won’t stand for this truth one iota? “Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?”
“I will teach you by the hand of God: that which is with the Almighty will I not conceal.” Job said I will teach you by the hand of God, and I’m not going to conceal it, I’m not going to hide it.
“Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?” Why are you in the midst of lies? Why are you deceitful?

“This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty.” Now he goes to the portion of a wicked man, and now we talk about white folks and the nations.
“If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword”: if the wicked’s children be multiplied, it is for the sword, meaning death. “And his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.”

“Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.” Job is saying the same thing David said in Psalms, the same thing Paul said in Thessalonians, the same thing John said in Revelation.

“Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay; He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on.” He may prepare it, but the just, Israel, shall put it on. Whatever this white man has prepared in terms of wealth and honor, it’s all being set up for us. “And the innocent shall divide the silver.”
“He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth that the keeper maketh”: it’s going to be destroyed. Their whole house is going to be knocked down.
“The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he is not”: meaning he’s dead. You got many of our people who follow the same steps as Esau.
“Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.”
“Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.”

precepts.why:
“I have also spoken by the prophets”: Job was a prophet. “And I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

So Job’s life was a similitude for us. Many of the things he spoke, and the things his friends spoke, are a similitude for us in these last days.

This is who the wicked is. “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

The people, not the man: it says the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. That’s the entire race. So when Job says “Let mine enemy be as the wicked”, our own people who rise up against this gospel are to be as Edom.

When he has gained, when God takes away his soul: Christ said that same thing. “For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Man, woman, boy, girl: if you gain everything in this world, fame, fortune, you gain it all, but you lose your soul, what has it profited you? Because the end is coming; the end is near.

Sure, you got your three billion dollars rich. You got women that come around you; you snap your fingers and they do your nails, they do your hair, they do everything for you. You got fame; everybody knows you.

That’s some of our brothers and sisters in the entertainment world. They have gained the world, fame and fortune, whatever they wanted they can get, and they will not stand for the truth of this Bible. They will not stand or support the sons and daughters of God Almighty, the prophets, the Israelites. But at the end, when they lose their soul, they’re going to think back on this message right here, this class they’re listening to right now.

What will you do when trouble comes? Will God hear your cry? “Because I have called, and ye refused; I have stretched out my hand, and no man regarded.” How does God stretch out his hand? Through us, the prophets, the teachers. And no man regarded: ‘ah, to hell with you Israelites.’

“But ye have set at nought all my counsel”: God’s counsel is the Bible, and you set the Bible at nought. “And would none of my reproof”: you didn’t want God’s laws at all.

“I also will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when your fear cometh.” So God does have a sense of humor. The God of heaven and earth said: you laughed at my sons and daughters, you laughed at the prophets, well, I’m gonna laugh too. “When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.”

“Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer”: then you’re gonna call on the Lord, but the Lord of heaven and earth will not answer. “They shall seek me early, but they shall not find me: For that they hated knowledge”: because you hated the Bible, “and did not choose the fear of the Lord.”

“Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.”

That’s why we teach everything. Everything the deacons and the Bishops know, y’all know; y’all are learning everything. We’re not concealing nothing. Men and women online, some of you watch, take our classes, refurbish them and give honor to your dumb elders. That’s all right, it’s all glory to the Lord. But we know who you are, and the Lord does too.

An example of the same judgment. This is about Esau: “When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers.”

Imagine this, brothers: you’re on the street teaching that the white man has committed adultery, that he has raped our mothers, our sisters, our aunts, our daughters from chattel slavery on up. Right. But now what about you, who have slept from woman to woman to woman and ain’t take care of not one? You’re getting the same judgment. You men, you Israelites online, understand that.

And they always find a woman being wicked: ‘oh, she’s wicked, that’s why I left her.’ You left 15 women and they were all wicked, brother? So when Esau gets hit, when his judgment comes, you wicked Israelites are gonna get the same judgment: death.

“Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.” Brothers, sisters, never be envious against evil men. You see evil men and they got riches, fame and fortune; don’t desire to be with them. “For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.” I hope you men and you women, everyone listening to the sound of my voice, understand that.

Here’s the precept to verses 14 and 15. “Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial”: the white man is not going to be joined with other nations in burial, “because thou hast destroyed thy land, and slain thy people”: this white man has destroyed his land and slain his citizens.

“The seed of evildoers shall never be renowned”: it’s calling them the seed of evildoers. They shall never be remembered. “Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers”: for the sins of their fathers, “that they do not rise, nor possess the land, nor fill the face of the world with cities.”

Job is saying the same thing David said in Psalms, the same thing Paul said in Thessalonians, the same thing John said in Revelation.

The precept to the just putting on what the wicked prepared: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.” Whatever wealth and honor this white man has heaped up is laid up for Israel, the just.

About our people. “And it came to pass, that the beggar died”: the 12 tribes of Israel died, “and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom”: that’s the elect of the 12 tribes.

“The rich man also died, and was buried”: our people who sided with Rome, who side with America, also died. “And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments”: in hell, destruction, he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, “and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.” That is the rich man of Job who opens his eyes and is not.

Terrors take hold on him. Here’s another parable, another similitude, another prophecy. “Terrors shall make him afraid on every side”: it’s gonna be bombs blowing up on every side, “and shall drive him to his feet.”

“Even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength”: Christ is the firstborn of death. “His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle”: Esau’s confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and his tabernacle is America. “And it shall bring him to the king of terrors”: Christ is the king of terrors.

“It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it is none of his”: destruction shall dwell in his tabernacle, because it’s not his; he stole it. “Brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off. His remembrance shall perish from the earth”: he’s going to be forgotten, “and he shall have no name in the street”: nobody’s gonna remember this white man’s name in the street.

“He shall be driven from light into darkness”: right now it appears that this white man is in light, but he’s going to be driven into darkness, “and chased out of the world.” “He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.” That’s what we just read in Isaiah 14:20-21, and what we read in Job 27. It’s all saying the same thing.

“Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished”: everyone’s going to be shocked, “and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.” They shall hiss: that’s what Job said, everyone’s going to hiss him out of his place.

“As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof”: just like Sodom and Gomorrah fell by fire and brimstone, so shall the United States of Babylon be overthrown by fire and brimstone. “No man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.” Nobody’s gonna abide here.

sense.text: “Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise”: that’s what David prayed, and that’s what we pray too.

“For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me.” Just as David said in this song, so do we say today. You got wicked like the ADL, the SPLC, the Canary Mission with their mouths open against us. Then you’ve got wicked of our own race, our own people, speaking against us, lying, saying we bring guns to reservations, we’re killing men, we’re killing women. “They have spoken against me with a lying tongue”: they speak against us with a lying tongue.

“They compassed me about also with words of hatred; and fought against me without a cause”: they fight against us for no reason. They start a fist fight: you can’t make this stuff up. Without a cause. Just because we get a crowd and you don’t, you want to physically fight us? Are you kidding me? How about repent and pray for the Holy Spirit, brother? How about keep God’s laws? It’s envy and jealousy.

We didn’t have to hurt nobody; we just subdued them. If we wanted to, we would have stomped him out. We didn’t stomp them out. Just hold them; don’t hurt the brother. That’s how we get down, because we’re not out there to harm our people. But if you bring it, we’re gonna bring the fire; we’re gonna hold you down.

“For my love they are my adversaries: but I give myself unto prayer.” Brothers, sisters, we give ourselves to prayer. We ask the Lord for mercy upon these wicked negro Israelite camps: be merciful upon them, O Father, they know not what they do.
“And they have rewarded me evil for good, and hatred for my love.”

“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” See what David is saying here: if they can’t repent, this is what’s going to happen. Satan is going to take over them one hundred percent, just as he did Cain. The white man is gonna roll with them.

“When he shall be judged, let him be condemned: and let his prayer become sin. Let his days be few; and let another take his office. Let his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.” “Let his children be continually vagabonds, and beg”: bums. “Let his posterity be cut off; and in the generation following let their name be blotted out.”
“Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered with the Lord; and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.” See, the white woman ain’t gonna escape either.
“Let them be before the Lord continually, that he may cut off the memory of them from the earth”: cut off their memory from the earth.

“Because that he remembered not to shew mercy”: this man remembered not to show mercy, “but persecuted the poor and needy man”: he persecuted the 12 tribes of Israel; that’s the poor and needy man. “That he might even slay the broken in heart”: that’s Israel. We are the broken in heart.

precepts.why: Satan taking over them just as he did Cain. This is what God told Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you do well, meaning keep God’s law, won’t you be accepted of me? “And if thou doest not well”: if you choose to be rebellious, Cain, if you blacks choose to be rebellious, “sin lieth at the door.” Sin lies at your door. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: all his desires are gonna be unto Satan.
Here’s the precept to Satan standing at his right hand: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders.”

Jump down to verse 12. This verse is talking about our people: “That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” We’re gonna get the same judgment. You’re not going to just say all the white man’s the devil while you’re breaking commandments and attacking God’s people. You’re gonna get the same judgment.

sense.text: We’re not finished with the forefather Job. “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.” Remember that: in all that Job went through, he did not sin, and he did not charge or blame God foolishly.

precepts.why:
Now this is Job speaking, humbling himself down. Surely it has to be something I’ve done: “I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?”

“And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity?” He was asking the Lord, why don’t you pardon my transgression, please take away my iniquity. “For now shall I sleep in the dust”: now shall I die. “And thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be”: Lord, I won’t be here in the morning.

Job did not charge God foolishly; he humbled himself and confessed his sin.

This is about repenting, humbling yourself down to the Lord. There’s another place where Job asks who ever died being innocent, meaning there’s no man and no woman that’s innocent upon this earth.

“We acknowledge, O Lord, our wickedness”: that’s what all of us got to do, acknowledge our wickedness, “and the iniquity of our fathers.” We also got to acknowledge the iniquity of our fathers, for we have sinned against the law. So the same suffering Job went through, we as a nation, as a people, have suffered likewise.

“Do not abhor us, for thy name’s sake”: don’t hate us, O Lord. “Do not disgrace the throne of thy glory: remember, break not thy covenant with us.”

sense.text: “Then Job answered the Lord, and said”. Pay close attention to Job’s answer.
“Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.” Job said, I repent in dust and ashes.

Pay close attention to this. “Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.” So everybody came to Job and brought him money.

Job’s life is our life, the life of the nation of Israel, and what was done for Job the nations are going to do for us.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: the wealth of the Gentiles. Just like Job’s friends, his brothers, everybody brought him wealth, the nations are going to do the same thing with us. “And that their kings may be brought.” All these nations are going to gather their wealth to bring it to us.
“For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”. All these nations, gathering gold and diamonds and wealth: all that is Bible prophecy of what they’re going to do for us, “to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee shall come bending unto thee; and all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet”. All they that despised us. The nations are going to come bending unto us. “And they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

“Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated”: we’ve been forsaken and hated. “So that no man went through thee”: no man cared for us. “I will make thee an eternal excellency, a joy of many generations”: he’s going to make us an eternal excellency, and we’re going to be a joy of many generations.

“Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles”: eating all their wealth, all their riches. “And shalt suck the breast of kings”: everything the kings got is ours. “And thou shalt know that I the Lord am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.”

“For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver”: the iron we got, he’s going to give us silver. For the wood we got he’s going to give us brass, and for the stones we got he’s going to give us iron.

“I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness.” An exactor is a tax collector. We are going to be the tax collectors of the earth: their silver, their gold, their brass, the iron. Everything is ours.

“Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: no more wars, no more fussing, no more fighting, no more stupid Black Hebrew Israelites trying to start a fight with us. No more. “Wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day”, because Christ is going to be our light. “Neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory.”

precepts.why: “And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there. And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it.” John the Revelator is saying the same thing Isaiah is saying, the same thing that happened to the forefather Job: the gates open, and the nations bringing their glory and honour in.

They shall call us the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel, and that was read earlier in Isaiah 1: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

Remember when Christ gave out the rewards: “Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” “And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds. And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.”

The nations are going to come bending unto us. Our people, you men, are going to rule this earth. We’re going to rule all nations, and you women understand that too: we are going to rule this planet in righteousness. That’s what the Bible says.

sense.text: Listen good. “He had also seven sons and three daughters.” Remember, Job lost his sons, and we lost our children.

“And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren–happuch.” Aunt Jemima on the pancake box: this is what they did to us. Little did we know that they were making mockery, because the Bible says Job’s daughter was Jemima, and these three girls were the most beautiful on the whole planet earth.

“And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job”. Our women are going to be like that: no blemishes, no pimples, no cellulite on the legs, no toes all jacked up, no crow’s feet. “And their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.”

“After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, even four generations. So Job died, being old and full of days.” Job got blessed, and what he did for Job, he’ll do for us.

precepts.why:
Listen good. “Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro?” We lost our children, talking about the two-thirds that’s going to be put to death here. But we’re going to get new sons, new daughters, just like Job.

“And who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?” These children, where did they come from, where have they been? “Thus saith the Lord God, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people”: watch this, they, the nations, shall bring them, and they “shall be carried upon their shoulders.”

This is how our women are going to be. “That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth”: our sons are going to be like plants. “That our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace”, meaning they’re going to be beautiful, they’re going to be lovely, just like Job’s daughters.

“And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles”: our sons and our daughters, our seed, are going to be known among the Gentiles, “and their offspring among the people.” Everybody is going to know our children. They’re going to show respect and move the hell out their way when they come down the street.

“All that see them shall acknowledge them”: every nation that sees our sons and daughters shall acknowledge them, “that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” That’s the prophecy; that’s what we’re going to get.

This is the gift we’re going to get. “For the wages of sin is death”: that’s what you’re going to get if you sin, brothers and sisters. “But the gift of God”, the gift of God that we all want, “is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” So Job got on it; Job got blessed.

Listen, brothers; listen, sisters. “Look at the generations of old, and see”: look at Job, he’s from the generations of old. “Did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Who abode in his fear, keeping the commandments, and was forsaken? “Or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?” Who did God ever despise that called upon him?

“For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.” What he did to Job, he’ll do for us.

“But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Put the images on the screen, us standing in front of the castles and all that: that is just what they come up with on the computer, but the prophecy says we can’t even imagine it.

“But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”, by his Holy Spirit: “for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” “Even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God.”

“Now we have received, not the spirit of the world”: brothers and sisters, we have not received the spirit of the world, “but the spirit which is of God”, the Holy Spirit, “that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God.” “Which things also we speak, not in the words which man’s wisdom teacheth”: we don’t speak in the wisdom of this world, man’s wisdom, “but which the Holy Ghost teacheth”. We speak as the Holy Ghost teaches us, “comparing spiritual things with spiritual”, meaning precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

“But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God”: the natural man is the sinful man, the carnal man. He does not believe the things of the Spirit of God, “for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.”
